samples.summary: New preview click-to-write path is authorized client-side only; the server-side gate it relies on is disabled by default
samples.evidence: This change turns the preview pane into a write surface: `onToggleTask: readOnly ? undefined : (line, checked) => setTaskChecked(view, line + 1, checked)` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:258-260). The ONLY thing distinguishing a viewer from an editor on this path is the client-side `readOnly` boolean, which comes from `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` in packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:323 — a value the browser controls. packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:119-120 asserts the backstop ("a read-only share viewer has no write permission — the auth webhook would reject the update"), and packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:255 repeats it ("A read-only mount passes no callback"). But the enforcement point, packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-105, is gated on `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'` and defaults to SHADOW mode: when the flag is unset it logs `[shadow] would deny ...` and returns `{ allowed: true }`. `hasAccess` (line 200) is the code that would actually reject a viewer (`needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`) and it is bypassed in shadow mode. Attacker chain: obtain any viewer-role share link, open the note, and issue a Yorkie `rw` update (devtools console against the attached document, or simply patch the client-side `readOnly` value) — the auth webhook returns allow and the edit persists to every collaborator. The write surface added here is new; the missing enforcement is pre-existing, which is why the comments claiming a server-side backstop are the concrete defect to fix (either flip enforcement or stop documenting an inactive gate as the guarantee).

samples.summary: New list commands and setTaskChecked dispatch document mutations with no readOnly/editable check, unlike the sibling handler added in the same change
samples.evidence: `replacePrefixes` (packages/notes/src/view/list-commands.ts:207-209) and `setTaskChecked` (line 295-300) call `view.dispatch(...)` unconditionally. Neither consults `view.state.readOnly` nor `view.state.facet(EditorView.editable)` — and CodeMirror's `EditorView.editable.of(false)` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:413), which is what `initialize(..., readOnly)` sets for every share-link mount, only blocks DOM-originated input; it does not block programmatic transactions. The five commands are then re-exported on the public `NoteEditorAPI` (editor.ts:581-585), which `initialize` hands to any host via `onEditorReady`, read-only mounts included. The same change adds `noteCheckboxInput` (packages/notes/src/view/checkbox-input.ts:24-30) which explicitly guards BOTH ways for exactly this reason, so the guard is inconsistent across the write paths introduced together. Today the only host is `NotesToolbar`, rendered solely from notes-detail.tsx:198 (always writable) and never from SharedNotesLayout, so I could not complete an exploit chain — hence low confidence. But `NotesToolbar`'s `readOnly` prop is optional and defaults to falsy (notes-toolbar.tsx:229, 252), so a future read-only host that renders the toolbar gets a fully functional write path on a document it may not write, with the engine offering no enforcement of its own.
searchedFor: read packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts in full (readOnly usages: lines 235, 240, 258, 334, 413)

samples.summary: Task checkboxes now render interactive by default and are only made inert by a post-hoc DOM pass, a fail-open default for read-only previews
samples.evidence: The module-level renderer was flipped from `md.use(taskLists, { label: true, enabled: false })` to `md.use(taskLists, { enabled: true })` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:53), so the shared `md` instance now emits non-disabled `<input class="task-list-item-checkbox">` for every caller. Read-only safety is restored only after the fact, inside `NotePreview.render()`, by `if (!this.onToggleTask) { for (const box of this.el.querySelectorAll(TASK_CHECKBOX_SELECTOR)) box.setAttribute('disabled', '') }` (lines 320-324), keyed on the string selector `input.task-list-item-checkbox` (line 24). The safe state is therefore opt-out rather than opt-in: any render of `md.render(...)` that does not go through `NotePreview.render` (or a markdown-it-task-lists upgrade that changes the checkbox class the selector matches) silently produces an interactive read-only preview. `md` is currently only consumed by this class, so there is no live exploit — but inverting the default (`enabled: !!this.onToggleTask` per instance, or enabling only on the interactive path) removes the fail-open shape entirely.
searchedFor: Grep 'innerHTML' in packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts to confirm async mermaid passes do not re-create checkbox markup

verdict.reason: All claimed code is present as described. editor.ts:253-261 adds a preview write path gated only by the client-side `readOnly` flag, which originates from `resolved.role === "viewer"` in shared-document.tsx:323 (browser-controlled). The documented server backstop (notes-view.tsx:118-120, editor.ts:253-255) is yorkie-auth.controller.ts, whose enforcement is gated on `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'` (line 86-87) and defaults to shadow mode: a deny decision is rewritten to HTTP 200 `{ allowed: true, reason: 'shadow' }` (lines 97-105), discarding the only viewer-vs-editor role check (`needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`, line 200). A repo-wide grep found no env/deployment file enabling enforcement, and auth.service.ts:36-78 issues share tokens with no role or verb scoping, so the webhook is the sole server-side enforcement point and Yorkie cannot distinguish viewer from editor on its own. A viewer-role share-link holder can therefore persist writes to all collaborators. This is a missing/weakened authorization gate on a write path — in the security lane and blocking; no guard elsewhere makes it unreachable, so no named refutation ground applies.

verdict.reason: The literal absence in list-commands.ts is real (no readOnly/editable check at the dispatch sites, lines 207-209 and 295-300), but the security claim — a write path a read-only principal can reach — is refuted: every entry point to those mutations is already gated on readOnly. setTaskChecked's only in-engine caller is `onToggleTask: readOnly ? undefined : ...` (editor.ts:258-260), and NotePreview neither binds the click handler nor enables the checkboxes without that callback (preview.ts:255, 320-322). The five list commands' only host, NotesToolbar, renders the whole formatting group (incl. bullet/ordered/task/indent/outdent at notes-toolbar.tsx:300-334) only when `canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== "view"` (notes-toolbar.tsx:252, gate at 257). The read-only share mount, SharedNotesLayout, passes no `onEditorReady` (shared-document.tsx:352), so no host ever receives the NoteEditorAPI on a read-only mount (NotesView only exposes it via onEditorReady, notes-view.tsx:134). Finally, the enforced authorization boundary is server-side: the Yorkie auth webhook grants write only to editor-role share links (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:164-168, 200), so a client-side command guard is not the enforced path in the first place. What is left is a hypothetical future host that renders the toolbar with readOnly unset — the reviewer concedes there is no exploit chain today — which is a design-consistency matter for the correctness lens, not an authorization bypass.
